Each time a bishop of Senj-Modruš sat down with this book, went through it, and signed that he had. *Whatever else is true of this register, it was inspected — which is part of why the silence in it can be trusted.*

**Images 4–80 done; 1871 read to entry 25.** The trades keep widening: 1871 alone has a **sutor** (cobbler), a **pictor** (painter) from Selce, three serving soldiers, and a **nauta of Portoré** — Kraljevica under its Italian name.

*A sixth magnified check: 1871 no. 15 read as a possible *Franc-* form and is **Matthaeus Franović, sutor**. Six checks in the first half, six different names. And 1871 no. 14, first read as «Istria», is **«Sponsus Portoregensis»**.*

**1872 and most of 1873 read. Images 4–86 done. 1872 closes at only 10 marriages — the thinnest year since 1865.**

**Three entries on these pages are worth having, and one of them puts an Italian surname and Ledenice on the same line for the first time.**

**1873 no. 8, magnified twice: «Pius Devalle, sutor»** — a cobbler — his origin written **«Sponsus Ledena[ice]»**. An Italian-surnamed shoemaker **out of Ledenice**, marrying at Crikvenica in February 1873. *He is not ours, and nothing here suggests he is.* But Ledenice is where **Anna Kalanj** was baptised in 1864, and this is the first time in the whole reading that an Italian name and that village appear together. It is logged for what it is: a fact about the place, not a link.

**1873 no. 9, magnified: «Dominus Josephus Pauricchi × Maria Braitenfeld», married *in articulo mortis*** — at the point of death — the union afterwards **ratified by the Ordinariate on 3 April**. A third Italian-form surname, a German one beside it, and a Ragusa connection in the parents' column. The parish register recorded even this, a deathbed marriage of two outsiders, in full.

**And Benedetti is still here.** He witnesses **1872 no. 7** and again **1873 no. 8**, each time written **«mercator in loco»**, once alongside a second merchant, **David Mansanari**. From 1868 to 1873 the same Italian merchant family keeps appearing, and the clerk keeps naming it.

*Also on these pages: **Josephus Jelinić, financiarius**, a revenue officer of Selce, married under indult of the **Supreme Financial Directorate** dated 11 November 1871, with **Vitus Cukić, officialis financiarius** standing witness. The Austrian state is now inside this village register too.*

**1873 and 1874 complete; 1875 begun. Images 4–94 done — the first half is two-thirds read.**

1873 closes at **19** marriages, 1874 at **23**. **No Defranceschi in any column of either.**

These are quiet years in the book and the entries are almost all Car, Brnjac, Župan, Matejčić, Benić, Ivančić and Jurinčić marrying each other across the villages of **Dolac, Draga, Supera, Sopaljska** and **Ludvić** — the same closed circle the 1880s pages showed. The one thing that keeps changing is the witness column, where the parish's small officialdom is now named: a **tabernarius communalis in loco** — the village innkeeper — a **miles pensionatus**, a communal officer, and beside them the merchants **Benedetti** and **Mansanari**.

**Remaining: images 95–123, the years 1875 to 1882.**

## The Montanari, four times across eleven years — and a correction to my own log.

**1875 closes at 19 marriages, 1876 at 23** — the priest writes the total himself: *«Anno 1876 copulati fuere 23. Sequitur annus 1877.»* **No Defranceschi in either.** Images 4–104 done.

**1876 no. 20, magnified: «Dnus Jacobus Pezelj, capitaneus maritimus» — a master mariner — marrying a daughter of DAVID MONTANARI.** The parents' column gives it plainly: *«Dftus Laurentius Pezelj & Maria nata Zelenčić — David Monta[nari] & …»*

That is the **fourth** appearance of this one Italian family in the volume:

| year | the entry |
|---|---|
| 1865 | **Maria-Anna Montanari** marries the clerk of the Vinodol district court |
| 1871 | **Eugenius Montanari** stands witness beside Benedetti, the merchant *in loco* |
| 1873 | **David Montanari** stands witness, *«mercator in loco»* |
| 1876 | **David Montanari's daughter** marries a master mariner |

**A correction to my own reading, made before it did any harm.** The 1873 witness I logged as *«David Mansanari»* is **David Montanari** — the same man, read properly at magnification. The scratchpad log carries the correction.

**This is what a family that actually lived in Crikvenica looks like in this book**: it arrives, it is written down with its trade, it witnesses its neighbours' weddings, and it marries its daughter off to a ship's captain — and the clerk records every stage. **Eighteen years of the register have now been read on both pages, 1859 to 1876, and our name has not once been written in any of them.**

**Remaining: images 105–123, the years 1877 to 1882.**

## The register changes language in January 1878 — and that closes the last gap in the reading.

**1877 closes at 16 marriages**, signed off *«Sequitur annus 1878. Crikvenica 31 decembris 1877. Alexander Car»*. **No Defranceschi.** Images 4–110 done; **thirteen images left.**

**At the head of 1878 the book stops being Latin and becomes Croatian.** *«Ljeta Gospodinova 1878, dne … siečnja»*; **poljodjelac** where it said *agricola*; **Rimo Katolik** spelled out; ages as *«zaručnik 20 godina, zaručnica 22 godine»*; status *«neoženjen / neudata»*. **Aleksandar Car** now signs as **župnik**, not *parochus*, and the observations cite the **Senj Ordinariat** and the Hungarian ministry in Croatian.

**Why this matters for the search, and not only as a curiosity.** The first half of this volume was read looking for **de Franceschi / Defranceschius** — the Latin nominative. From 1878 onward the same eye must look for **Defranceschi / Defranceski**, the Croatian form that the 1880s and 1890s pages use. **The changeover happens inside this reading, and both forms have now been searched for in the years where each was the one the clerk would have written.** There is no seam in the evidence where a differently-spelled name could have slipped through.

**And in 1878 the trade that ends this book begins.** 1878 no. 7: **«Mate Kristofor, zidar»** — the first **mason** in the register. By 1899 nearly every groom on the page is a *zidar*; here is the first of them.

*Also on these pages: **Mate Matejčić, domobranac** — a Croatian home-guardsman, married under leave of the royal Hungarian ministry, the state and its languages arriving together.*

---

# The volume is read. All 272 images, both pages, 1859 to 1908 — and the name is not in it.

**1880 closes at 12 marriages, 1881 is read to entry 8, and image 123 was the last image of this film that had never been looked at.** With it, **every one of the 272 images is read**, and a check against the log confirms there is no gap: *missing images: none.*

**Fifty years of one parish's marriages, on both pages of every entry.** Groom, bride, both sets of parents with the mothers' maiden names, two witnesses with their fathers' names and trades, the celebrant, the banns, the dispensations and the observations. **Not one Defranceschi, in any spelling, in any of those roles, in any year.**

**And the one debt this reading declared against itself is now paid.** Early on I recorded that **1888 entries 16 and 17 had never been seen**, falling between images 157 and 158. They have now been found and read: they are the **first two rows of image 158**, which a previous session numbered 18 and 19.

- **1888 no. 16** — **Petar Kalnić**, of the **pomorska oblast na Rieci**, the maritime authority at Rijeka, marrying **Ivana Wessel of Ljubljana**, 25 October 1888.
- **1888 no. 17** — Mikula Car and Marija Car, *radnici*, 21 November 1888.

**Which means a correction to this archive's own figures: 1888 closes at 17 marriages, not 19.** The names in that year were right; the count was two too many. *It is recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because the point of reading a volume end to end is that the arithmetic can be checked.*

## What fifty years of this register actually shows

**The parish was not closed to strangers, and it wrote every one of them down.** Across the volume the clerk recorded, with trade and birthplace attached: a district-court clerk and his wife **Maria-Anna Montanari** (1865); **Antonius Benedetti of Fiume**, merchant, and his Slovene bride (1868); **Pius Devalle**, an Italian-surnamed cobbler out of **Ledenice** (1873); **Josephus Pauricchi**, married *in articulo mortis* (1873); master mariners, a schoolmaster from Lokve, a revenue officer, a **Galician** clerk's son, a **Jewish-named** groom, a **Serbian Orthodox** sailor from Korenica, a locksmith from **Novi Sad**, **Franjo Ivan Pagliaga of Bakar**, son of **Vittoria** — and Hungarians, Bosnians, Carniolans and Krk islanders by the dozen.

**Two Italian families settled and stayed.** The **Benedetti** appear five times between 1868 and 1880 — arriving from Fiume, trading *in loco*, witnessing their neighbours' weddings, and finally marrying a daughter, **Jolanda Katarina Benedetti**, in February 1880. The **Montanari** appear four times between 1865 and 1876, ending with **David Montanari's** daughter marrying a master mariner.

**That is the shape of the negative, and it is as strong as a negative gets.** This register had the vocabulary, the occasion and the habit of writing Italian names down in full. It did so for two families over two decades. **It never once had cause to write ours.**

**Seven look-alikes were magnified rather than guessed at** — *Frašić, Koštrulja, Ivančić, Dračić, Franović, Marohnić* and one origin that read as *Zara* and is *Parochia Selcensis*. **Every one came back a different name.** And the volume changes language inside the reading — Latin to 1877, Croatian from January 1878 — so **both *de Franceschi* and *Defranceschi* were searched for in the years where each was the form the clerk would have used.** There is no seam where a differently-spelled name could have slipped through.

## What this closes, and what it does not

**It closes Crikvenica.** The marriage of **Josip Defranceschi and Anna Kalanj** is not in this book, and neither is any other bearer of the name, in fifty years. That is not a sample; it is the whole volume.

**It does not close the question.** Anton Rudolf was born at **Klenovica on 20 January 1890**, so his parents married by 1889, and the search now stands where this reading has left it: **Novi Vinodolski**, the parish that actually served Klenovica; **Ledenice after 1882**, whose later volumes are not on film; and **Bribir or Grižane**, the neighbours whose people marry into these very pages. Those are letters to write and registers to order, not films to read.

*Item 130 is done.*

rows.what: The Kriegsarchiv says the army records may already be digitised — and nobody has looked
rows.note:
**Vienna answered the 14 September enquiry by quoting for the sailors and declining the soldiers**, and the decline is the more useful half. For *Angehörige der Landstreitkräfte* the Kriegsarchiv points at its own **«Kriegsarchiv Forschungstipps (FAQ)»**, saying it already holds numerous tips for self-study online *«worunter auch alle bereits digitalisierten Bestände fallen»* — **including every holding already digitised.**

**Four men of the name are waiting in that half.** **Theodor Defranceschi**, k. k. Landwehr, Fähnrich (nichtaktiv), 27th Regiment, seniority 1 January 1907. **Alois Defranceschi**, k. u. k. Heer infantry cadet, in the rank lists 1916–1918. **Eduard Defranceschi**, k. k. line infantry, cadet 1859 and Unterleutnant 2. Klasse 1863 — **and whether that is one man or two is still open**. And **Dr Cäsar Peschle**, Landwehr medical officer from 1 August 1895.

**What is wanted from each is the same single fact**: the *Geburtsort*. The printed rank lists give the year of birth and never the place, which is precisely why not one of these men can be attached to a household.

*Free, online, and never once opened.* The paid navy search on Julius and Valentin is [a separate decision](/errands/) and costs €45 whether it finds anything or not.

---

**Done, 20 September, and it went further than the four soldiers.** The digitised holdings Vienna pointed at turned out to include **the whole ÖStA catalogue as a free name search** — `archivinformationssystem.at/feldsuche.aspx`, no account. One query returns **99 records on the stem, 53 of them this name**: AVA 19, FHKA 12, HHStA 11, Kriegsarchiv 7, AdR 4. [The full inventory is on the research log](/research-log/).

**On the four soldiers themselves the answer is mostly bad news, and worth knowing.** Officers' *Qualifikationslisten* 1870–1918 are filmed and on FamilySearch (Hauptreihe A–Z), **but lists of officers who took successor-state citizenship after 1918 were handed over to those states**. NCOs' and men's *Grundbuchsblätter* were kept **decentrally**: for the **Küstenland — Trieste, Istria, Görz-Gradisca — birth years 1860–1900 are at the Archivio di Stato di Trieste**, not Vienna; and for the **lands of the Hungarian crown, including Croatia-Slavonia, none survive at all**. **Theodor, Alois and Dr Peschle are therefore to be sought in Trieste or Zagreb before Vienna**, and that is a finding the €45 would not have bought.

**Eduard, 1859–1863, is the one still fully open in Vienna** — the pre-1868 *Abgangs-Verzeichnisse* are name-searchable online for all Truppenkörper and the *Grundbuchblätter* themselves are browsable, both filmed by FamilySearch. That is the next sitting, and it is free.

rows.what: The flag patents — the name is in the Habsburg merchant-marine registers from 1759
rows.note:
**`Erteilung der Flaggenpatente, Scontrini und Passavanti, nach Namen`** — a Hofkammer series that registers who was allowed to fly the imperial flag, arranged **by name**, and the entry reads *«… Fiumaner Handelskompagnie 1751-1787 … **Franceschi 1759-17..** …»*.

**This archive has an [at-sea page](/at-sea/) built out of masters' certificates and a Cardiff marriage, and it starts in the nineteenth century.** A flag patent is the licence a shipowner held. If the name is in this series from **1759**, the family's maritime life is a century older than anything published here, and it is documented in Vienna rather than inferred.

**The company named beside it matters too.** The *Fiumaner Handelskompagnie*, 1751–1787, is the Fiume trading company — the very port this archive keeps circling. **The signature, pulled the same afternoon: `AT-OeStA/FHKA NHK Kommerz Lit Akten 946`** — carton 1752–1791, former reference 5.377 / r.Nr. 637, *Faszikulatur 113 F*, protection expired 1821, **public and permission-free**. And the dates are exact: **Franceschi 1759–1770**.

**The series is the point.** *Kommerz Litorale, 1705–1813* is the Hofkammer's commerce administration **for the Austrian Littoral** — Trieste and Fiume. A *Flaggenpatent* is the licence to fly the imperial flag on a merchant ship; *scontrini* and *passavanti* are the clearance papers that go with it. **So a Franceschi was licensed to trade under the imperial flag out of the Littoral between 1759 and 1770** — a hundred years before the earliest master's certificate on [the at-sea page](/at-sea/), and sitting in the same carton as the **Fiumaner Handelskompagnie, 1751–1787**.

rows.what: A copy of the arms, dated 13 May 1825, in the Austrian nobility archive
rows.note:
**The [arms page](/arms/) rests on a lintel and a stone.** The Adelsarchiv holds paper.

**AT-OeStA/AVA Adel HAA AR 251.11 and 251.12** are *Adelsbestätigungen* of **24 May 1825** for **«Franceschi, Niklas, Markus, Johann Baptist, de»** and **«Franceschi, Mark Anton, de»** — the genitive spelling, in scope. **AR 251.13** confirms **Vinzenz Franceschi**, 25 June 1830; **AR 251.14**, **Philipp**, 1838–39.

**And AR 251.15 is the one to open first**: a request of 1897 for *«Ausfertigung eines Adelszertifikates und einer **Wappenkopie**, dato 13.05.1825»* — **a copy of the coat of arms**, made from an 1825 original. Behind it sit **AR 251.9** (Jakob von Franceschi, Dutch knighthood, 1608), **AR 251.10** (Thomas von Franceschi, 1610) and **RAA 119.29** (Michael Angelo Franceschi of Lucca, 1550, *Adelsstand, Wappenbesserung*).

**One honest deflation, checked before publishing it.** AR 251.15's own catalogue entry reads **«Wappen: nein · Siegel: nein»** and *Extent: fol. 1–6* — so the 1897 file is the **request** for the certificate and the arms copy, not the drawing. The arms it refers back to are the **13 May 1825** original, and that is what would have to be traced.

**A fifth document may matter more than all of them.** **AT-OeStA/HHStA KA Vertrauliche Akten 56-1-49** — *«Nr. 49: Marchese Johann Maria Gravisi, **Nicolaus De Franceschi**»*, **1825**, fol. 229–243, fifteen folios in the **confidential files of the Kabinettsarchiv**. The Gravisi were marquises of Capodistria. A De Franceschi named beside one of them in a confidential imperial file, in the same year as the nobility confirmations, is Istrian politics rather than genealogy — and this archive has never had a document of that kind.

*Whether any of these is this family is exactly the question. All are public and permission-free.*

rows.what: Pietro Franceschi wanted a post at Almissa in 1828, and Almissa is Omiš
rows.note:
**AT-OeStA/AVA Justiz OJSt JS DS 83.1.14 — «Franceschi, Pietro, Praktikantenstelle in Almissa», 1828–1843.** *Almissa* is the Italian name of **Omiš**, and [the Omiš line](/omis-line/) is one of this archive's six.

It does not stand alone. The Austrian justice administration holds a **cluster of Dalmatian officials of the name**: **JS DS 80.3.4**, *Franceschi, Antonio*, 1843; **JM Präs. A 140.14**, *«Franceschi, Giovanni Pietro **de**, Personalstandesausweis»*, 1876–1881; and **JM Präs. A 134.22**, **Carl Dragutin Defranceschi, born 29 July 1883 at Zara, judge at the district court of Šibenik**, 1909–1918.

**Four men of the name in the courts of Dalmatia across eighty years** — Omiš, Zadar, Šibenik. A *Personalstandesausweis* and a *Prospetto dello stato personale* both give birthplace, parents and career. *Found 20 September; none of the four is in this archive.*

rows.what: Johann Defranceschi of Gallignana, born 1833 — a sailor out of the origin parish
rows.note:
**Gallignana is Gračišće**, the Istrian parish this family comes out of and whose registers open in 1644. The Kriegsarchiv holds **three files** on a man born there in **1833** and none of them was known here.

**AT-OeStA/KA Marine NMA Pers OffBea Akten MGBBl 2651**, **VerEv Kdi 219** and **VerEv KL-Mardi 76** — *Defranceschi, Johann, geb. 1833, Geburtsort Gallignana*. The rank moves across the three: **Marinediener 4. Klasse** on one, **1. Klasse** on the other two, so a career is legible from the catalogue alone. The protection term on the last expired **31 December 1933**; all three are marked public, no permission required.

**A Marinegrundbuchblatt gives birthplace, parents, religion, marriage and children.** For a man born at Gračišće in 1833 that is a household — and the Gračišće baptism of 1833 is what would match against it.

**20 Sept 2026 — both searchable routes tried, both empty, and one of them does not exist.** The index holds forty-five Defranceschi births for **1825–1842** in Croatia and **not one is at Gračišće**; there is no Johann or Giovanni born 1833 in the set. And **Gračišće is not on film** — it is not a parish in the collection, only Pazin, Stari Pazin and Lupoglav are, and this archive's own atlas has carried `nfilms: 0` for it all along. The sentence that said otherwise has been corrected.

**The route that works is a named request to DAPA Pazin** — *Johann/Giovanni Defranceschi, Gračišće (Gallignana), born 1833* — the same shape of request they answered once before for 117 kuna. **That can go in the same envelope as the ÖStA order for MGBBl 2651**, and between them a Marinegrundbuchblatt and a baptism would give the man two independent households.

rows.what: Svetvinčenat — the castle the name never left, and Antonio's exemption of 1780
rows.note:
**This archive has six lines and none of them is San Vincenti.** *Atti* 48 (2018), from the Centro di ricerche storiche at Rovigno, says something no source here has ever said: *«Il cognome **Defranceschi** era stato l'unico ad avere nel **Castello di San Vincenti** una continuità…»* — **of all the surnames in the castle of San Vincenti, this one alone was continuous.**

**And it acted as a body.** *«Guidati da **Antonio Defranceschi**, nel **1780** avevano ottenuto l'esonero dal partecipare alla difesa armata»* — led by Antonio Defranceschi, in 1780 they got themselves excused from armed defence duty. That is a **household group with a spokesman and a privilege**, in a named place, in a named year.

**Svetvinčenat is twenty-five kilometres from Gračišće** and it is in the same Pazin county this archive's oldest registers come out of. Whether it is a branch, the parent stock, or an unrelated household of the name is exactly the question a one-name study exists to ask.

**What to do:** read the *Atti* 48 article itself for its footnote — the 1780 exemption will rest on a Venetian document, and Venetian Istria's records are at Pazin and Venice. The Svetvinčenat parish registers are the other half.

**20 Sept 2026 — the register is filmed, and it goes back to 1568.** Svetvinčenat is a parish in the FamilySearch Croatia collection (`9R2H-DPJ:391644801,392404501`) with **ten volumes**: births **1568–1588**, 1589–1646, 1663–1708, 1709–1764 and **1764–1791 + 1815–1874**; marriages 1581–1589/1622–23 and **1762–1858**; deaths 1791–1887 and 1887–1917. Unlike Gračišće it needs no letter and no fee. **This archive has already read 1666–1707 off DGS 005497884** — nineteen openings, band by band — so what was open ground is the **1709–1764** and **1764–1791** books, the next two on that shelf.

**Antonio's 1780 is already bracketed.** Births 1764–1791 is `9R2H-PTL:…392405201`, 369 images; **image 92 is «Anno D.ni 1782, Die 5 Januarij»**, so at about ten frames a year **1780 is near image 72**. Read out from there for the name, and read the marriages from 1762 beside it — a household that held a castle continuously should be thick on both.

**Caveat:** the **1568 volume is torn**; the film's card says so and the first leaf photographed has lost a third of its text. The clean run starts with 1709–1764.

**And then it was read.** One frame — **image 81 of Births 1764–1791** — carries two Defranceschi households at the font in 1780: **«Dominicus Defranceschi, et Fosca Uxor ejus»** on 16 April, and **«Mathea uxor Antonij Defranceschi»** on 1 May. **The *Atti* article's Antonio of 1780 is a man on a page.** Both are godparent appearances, not baptisms of their own children, and nothing yet ties either household to the Gologorica–Gračišće line. **Next:** read outward from image 81 for Defranceschi baptisses, marriages and burials of their own, and work back through 1709–1764 to see how far the continuity the article claims actually runs.

**And back another fifty-two years.** The 1709–1764 births volume carries **its own contemporary index** at the back (images ~197–214), arranged **by the child's forename** — sixteen images instead of two hundred, and on those frames an index leaf faces a register leaf so both pages must be read. Its **C** page gives **«Cattarina fig.a di D.o Batta Defranceschi 11 Feb.ro 1728 — c. 66»**, and carta 66 (image 77, right page) has the entry in full: **«Catta fig.a leg.ma di S.r Batta de Fran.chi et di Anzoletta sua Consorte, nata li 10 d.to… Padrini… il S.r Bortolo Francal Giudice et la S.ra Madalena moglie del Sig. Vic.o Quelis»**. **A Defranceschi household in the castle in 1728, styled *Signore*, with the village judge as godfather.**

**The method now scales.** Scan the rest of that index for every Defranceschi line; then see whether **1663–1708** and **1589–1646** carry indexes of their own — if they do, the *Atti* article's claim of continuity can be tested back to 1589 for the cost of a few dozen screenshots. **Marriages 1762–1858 has not been touched.**

**A second household, and a man followed across thirty-two years.** The index's **D** page gives **«Dom.co Gasparo di Giacomo Defranceschi 9 Ag.to 1732 — c. 80»**, and the register leaf facing that same index page — baptisms of **February 1764** — has as godfather **«D. Gasparo de Franceschi figlio di Giacomo»**. **The child of 1732 standing at the font himself at thirty-one.** So the castle holds **Batta × Anzoletta** (1728), **Giacomo** (1732), **Gasparo son of Giacomo** (1764), **Dominicus × Fosca** and **Antonius × Mathea** (both 1780) — fifty-two years of the name without leaving one volume. **Carta 80 has not been opened**, and the rest of the index (A, B, E, F, G, I, L, N, O, R, S, T, V, Z) has not been read.

**Index letters C–G now read.** The **G** page adds the earliest child yet — **«Gasparo di Batta Defranceschi 10 Agosto 1718 — c. 31 t°»** — so **Batta** has two children in the book (Gasparo 1718, Cattarina 1728) and **Giacomo** one (Domenico Gasparo 1732). **Each father names a son Gasparo**, which in this parish's naming habit would make them brothers, sons of a Gasparo older than the volume — *inference from a naming pattern only.* **Still to read: index letters A, B, I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z**, and cartas 31 t° and 80.

**B page: a third child and the father's name in full.** **«Battistina fig.a di Gio Batta Defranceschi 23 Xbre 1731 — c. 76 t°»** — so «Batta» is **Gio Batta, Giovanni Battista**, with three children in the book (Gasparo 1718, Cattarina 1728, Battistina 1731) beside Giacomo's one. **And a warning for whoever sweeps these books next:** the same page carries *«Battista fig.o di m.ro Piero **Defranzieri** 7 mag.o 1712»*, which reads like the name in a list and is not it — magnified, **‑ieri** against **‑eschi**. Dissolved. **Letters read: B, C, D, E, F, G. Left: A, I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z.**

**Sweep state, so it can be picked up cleanly.** The index of Births 1709–1764 occupies film images **~196–214**, and on most frames an index leaf faces a register leaf, so both pages of each frame must be looked at. **Read: images 197, 198, 199, 200, 201, 202, and the right page of 207** — letters **B, C, D, E, F, G** and the 1720–23 stretch of **M**. **Unread: 196, 203, 204, 205, 206, 207 left, 208–211, 212 (P), 213, 214** — letters **A, I, L, most of M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z**, which is where Antonio, Domenico, Lucia, Maria, Nicolò, Pietro and Zuanne would be.

**Three cartas are named by the index and still unopened: 31 t°, 76 t° and 80.** Opening them would give mothers, godparents and trades for Gasparo 1718, Battistina 1731 and Domenico Gasparo 1732, the way carta 66 did for Cattarina.

**A correction this item has to carry.** The rows written for it on 20 September announced the parish as untouched — *«nobody here has opened it»*, *«a sixth Istrian parish»*, then *«a seventh»*. **All false.** The work-list sentence *«this archive has six lines and none of them is San Vincenti»* is about **lines**, not records, and was misread as meaning the parish was unread. The archive holds **seventy-five people** there, a **1628** baptism, `nfilms: 9`, and *«twelve distinct fathers of this surname in one small town between 1657 and 1737»*. **What is genuinely new is everything after 1707.**

**And a conflict to settle before anything is merged.** The families page carries *«1733 Maria, of **Giacomo** and Anzoletta»*; carta 66 gives *«**Batta** de Fran.chi et di Anzoletta»* in **1728**. **Two husbands for one forename.** Cartas 80 and the 1733 entry both name the mother and neither has been opened.

**20 Sept, later — L and the head of M read, and M paid.** **«Maria d' m.ro Nardo defranceschi, 13 Agosto 1709 — c. 13 t°»** and **«Marina di Piero Defranceschi, 21 Febraro 1710 — c. 6»**. **Both are after 1707**, which is precisely the stretch this item called genuinely new.

*Maria continues Nardo's house* — the one with the boy Piero baptised twice in October 1707 on a mother Eufemia. *Marina opens another*: her father **Piero** cannot be that infant, so he is an older man, and **«Ant.o di Franceschi di Piero» of 1667** is the same forename a generation or two back. Open.

**L is clean** — ninety lines of Lucia and Lorenzo, 1711–1733, no De Franceschi. Recorded so it is not read twice.

**A third, on image 205: «Maria di Batto Defranceschi, 13 Luglio 1716 — c. 26»** — **the earliest child of Batta's household**, two years before Gasparo of 1718. *Carta 26 would give the mother, which bears on the Batta/Giacomo conflict this item already carries.*

**Letters read: B, C, D, E, F, G, L, and M through 1717 — images 203, 204, 205. Left: A, I, the rest of M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V, Z** — images **196 and 206–213**. Arks for index images 190–213 are in `scratchpad/svetvincenat/index-arks-190-213.lst`.

**Cartas now wanted: 6, 13 t°, 26, 31 t°, 76 t°, 80** — five register leaves that would give mothers, godparents and trades.

**21 Sept — the index is read end to end, and it stops at P.**

**It occupies images 196–211 and runs B, C, D, E, F, G, L, M, N, O, P.** Image 195 is register text so **there is no A**; image 212 is a loose certificate and 213 the **«END OF ITEM»** card so **there is no R, S, T, V or Z**. *The earlier list of «letters left» assumed pages that do not exist.*

**That is a trap aimed at this family:** the index cannot reach **Antonio** or **Zuanne** — the two forenames this parish is known for here. **A nil from this index is not a nil from the register.**

**Seven entries found, five households.** New fathers **Nadal** (Natale, *not* Nardo) and **Piero**. Full table on [the search register](/searched/).

**And the Batta/Giacomo conflict is closed.** **Carta 66 carries both** — Batta's *Cattarina* on **10 February 1728** and Giacomo's *Maria* on **11 February 1728**, one day apart on the same leaf. **Two different men**, and Anzoletta was carried from one entry to its neighbour.

**What is left on this item is no longer the index. It is eight register leaves:** **cartas 6, 13 t°, 26, 31 t°, 66, 76 t°, 80 and 83** — mothers, godparents and trades — and then **a page-by-page read for the unindexed letters**, which is the only way to reach an Antonio.

---

**21 September, second pass: seven of the eight leaves are open, and they pay better than the index did.** [The reading is on the search register](/searched/). Three mothers — **Vittoria** (Piero, 1710), **Elena** (Giacomo, 1728), **Anzoletta** (Giacomo, 1733); a **sixth man of the name**, *«il sig.r Marcio de Franceschi»*, godfather twice in seven weeks in 1709–10 and **structurally invisible to an index arranged by the child's forename**; and **«D. Nadal Defraneschi»** godfather in 1732, four entries above a **«Nadal Venir»** on the same leaf.

**It also cost a published claim.** This morning's note called the 1733 Anzoletta a clerk's carry-over; [carta 83 says her name in its own hand](/corrections/), first entry on the leaf, nothing to carry from.

**And the index's page numbers are not safe.** *«Marina di Piero, 21 Febraro 1710 — c. 6»* is **carta 16**. **Carta 76 t° and carta 26 are now open too.** 76 t° gives **Battistina, born 18 and baptised 23 November 1731 to Gio Battista and *Maria*** — a month earlier than the index said and a mother it did not give. **Carta 26 runs 18 April to 22 June 1716 and carries no Defranceschi at all**, so the index's *«13 Luglio 1716 — c. 26»* has nothing behind it. **Three of the index's four page references have now failed.**

**The wives resolve into two men who each married twice** — Gio Battista: Anzoletta then Maria; Giacomo di Pietro: Elena then Anzoletta. *Anzoletta* sits in both households twenty years apart, which is the whole of the confusion.

**Still to open: carta 31 t°** (Gasparo, 1718) — and it should be found **by date, not by carta**. Then the page-by-page read for the letters the index never had, which remains the only route to an Antonio.

---

**The page-by-page read has begun, in the right volume.**

**Antonio's exemption is 1780, and 1780 is in the *second* births volume (1764–1791), not the one whose index was swept.** Frames **81, 82, 83** are read — 21 April to late October 1780 — and they give **«Matthea uxor Antonij Defranceschi»** on carta 80 and **«Dominico Defranceschi»** as godfather on carta 82/83. **No child of the name is baptised in any of them.**

**Do not resume at frame 84 — it is January 1763.** Frames 81–83 are April–October 1780 and frame 84 jumps **seventeen years backwards**, on consecutive film frames (`005497885_00295`–`00298`). [The film does not run in date order here](/corrections/), and both years were verified at magnification. **Date every frame from its own heading; never infer one from a frame number.** Arks for images 71–110 are in `scratchpad/svetvincenat/vol1764-arks-71-110.txt`, and the two-call-per-frame spread crop is recorded [with its own warning](/method/). The 1781–1791 leaves have still to be found, and finding them now means probing for them rather than walking forward.

**Still to do**: the rest of 1764–1791, carta 31 t° of the first volume (found by date, not by carta), and the first volume's unindexed letters.

---

**Seven spreads read, and the silence redirects the search.**

Images 81–83 (1780) and 93–95 (Dec 1781 – Feb 1782) carry **three Defranceschi and all three are godparents** — Matthea, Dominico, Jusca. **No baptism of the name in any of them.** [The reading is on the search register](/searched/).

**A godparent is an established adult, so the children were born earlier.** The generation to hunt is **1750–1775** — the end of the first volume and the opening of the second — **not the years around the exemption**. That is where the next pass should go, and it is a different place from where this one was heading.

**The 1750–1763 window is now bracketed.** Image **160** is carta 143, October 1751 – February 1752; image **185** is carta 168, June–October 1761 and **in Italian, not Latin**; image 195 is the last register leaf before the index. At ~3.26 images a year that puts the whole window at **images 149–195, about forty-seven frames**. Both probes were nil. Arks are in `scratchpad/svetvincenat/vol1709-arks-151-196.txt`.

**And the spread crop has now produced four false positives in one session** — *Dassanich*, *Blasan*, *Jurca uxor Antonij*, and *Defranzieri* from the earlier sweep. **It has never once confirmed a name correctly.** It is a finding tool only.

**And the index has already narrowed the read to eight forenames.** It holds seven Defranceschi entries and **all seven are 1734 or earlier**, in a volume running to 1763. It covers **B–P**, so if children of the name exist in 1735–1763 they are called **Antonio, Andrea, Anzolo, Rocco, Simon, Tomaso, Vito or Zuanne** — and *Antonio* is the man the item exists for. [The reasoning is on the search register](/searched/). **Image 165 is carta 148, 1754**, and the rate there is about two images a year, not the 3.26 extrapolated from the 1734–1761 span — so use the anchors, not the average.

---

**Blocked mid-read: the FamilySearch session dropped.**

The waypoint call began returning **503** and the tab was redirected to `ident.familysearch.org/en/identity/login/?state=…/search/film/005497885`. **This archive does not enter credentials**, so the register work stops here until David signs in again.

**Everything needed to resume in one move is written down.** The next step is **not** the forty-seven-frame baptism sweep — it is the **marriages, 1762–1858** (waypoint `9R28-YWT:391644801,392404501,392405601`), which was being opened when the session went. **A marriage register names the groom's father**, and Antonio's marriage to Matthea would settle in one entry what the baptisms would take a week to circle. Marriages are also far thinner than baptisms, so it is a smaller book to read.

**If the marriages give nothing**, fall back to the baptism sweep with the anchors already pinned — images 160 (1751–52), 165 (1754), 185 (1761), 195 (last leaf) — and **look for eight forenames, not for a surname**.

---

**Signed in again, and the marriage register was the right call.**

The marriages **1762–1815** (the title card's dates; the catalogue says 1862–1858) are open for the first time. **Carta 11, 9 February 1766: *«Elena figlia di q. Mattio de Franceschi, nativa di questo Castello»* marries **Mattio Sandalezza of Albona**.** [The reading is on the search register](/searched/).

**A ninth man of the name — and dead before 1766.** One leaf of marriages reached the generation that seven spreads of baptisms could not. **Continue here**: front matter runs to image 5, register text starts at image 6, and image 15 is carta 11 (1765–66). Arks 1–45 are in `scratchpad/svetvincenat/marriages-1762-arks-1-45.txt`.

**Eight marriage frames read, and the volume is twice the size the catalogue implies.** **It is at least 85 images, not the 45 a single waypoint call returns** — ask for `start=45` as well. **1762–1779 occupies images 6–44; 1780–1815 is 45–85, and there is no index at the back of the first part.**

Date anchors now pinned: img 6 = Nov 1762, 7 = Dec 1762–Mar 1763, 15 = carta 11 (1765–Feb 1766), 16 = May–Jul 1766, 17 = Aug 1766–Jun 1767, 18 = Jul–Nov 1767, 19 = Nov 1767–Jan 1768, 44 = carta 39 (1778–79). **The register switches Italian → Latin around image 16 and back to Italian by image 44.**

**Read and nil: 6, 7, 16, 17, 18, 19, 44. Still to read for a pre-1780 Antonio: images 8–14 and 20–43** — thirty-one frames. Arks 1–85 are in `scratchpad/svetvincenat/marriages-1762-arks-1-45.txt`.

rows.what: A Glagolitic inscription at Gologorica, in the standard corpus, tied to the name
rows.note:
**Branko Fučić's *Glagoljski natpisi* (JAZU, Zagreb 1982) is the corpus of Croatian Glagolitic inscriptions** — the reference work, not a byway. It contains this: *«Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u **Gologorici**, gdje su **Defranceschi**…»* — the inscription was probably recorded at Gologorica, **where the Defranceschi…**

**Gologorica is one of this archive's own origin places** — the Gologorica and Gračišće line, whose registers open in 1644. **A Glagolitic inscription connected to the name, at that village, in the standard scholarly corpus, and there is not one line about it on this site.**

**Why it could matter more than a register entry.** Glagolitic is the Croatian liturgical script, and an inscription is stone or a book-margin note — **it is older than any parish register in this archive and it is in the other language.** A family that appears in Italian on Venetian paper and in Glagolitic on an Istrian wall is the whole argument of [the name page](/name/) in one object.

**Most of the sentence has since been recovered**, by walking the full-text index phrase by phrase — each search re-centres the snippet, so the sentence can be read a few words at a time out of a book whose pages are closed for copyright:

> *«Riječ »**Pomjane**« (ime istarskog sela) ne može se čitati u posljednjem retku. Natpis je vjerojatno registriran u **Gologorici**, gdje su **Defranceschi imali posjed i** …»*

— *«The word »Pomjane« (the name of an Istrian village) cannot be read in the last line. The inscription was probably registered at **Gologorica**, where the **Defranceschi had an estate and** …»*

**Two things fall out of that, and the second is the bigger.** **Pomjane** is a village name this archive has never held — it is the word Fučić could not read on the stone. And **«imali posjed»** is not a mention, it is a **landholding**: Fučić places the family as **proprietors at Gologorica**, and dates the inscription by that fact rather than the other way round.

**What is still needed is the last clause and the entry's apparatus** — the inscription's catalogue number, its date, its reading and where the stone or page now is. The walk stops at *«posjed i»*; the rest is in the printed book. **NSK, *Glagoljski natpisi*, Fučić, JAZU 1982** — a reading-room hour, or a reproduction order from `digitalna.nsk.hr`. *Walked 20 September 2026.*

**20 Sept — dated, and deflated.** Gologorica's Glagolitic record: an inscription on a discarded **holy-water vessel base of 1549** at the All Saints chapel; **graffiti of the 15th–16th century** on the north wall of the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary *kod lokve*; and the **1595** inscription of the priest **Juraj Kaligarić** in the north chapel of SS Peter and Paul.

**But nothing found says the family is named in any of them.** The fragment that opened this item reads as though it did; the likelier completion is *«…where the Defranceschi had their house»* — the family as the **place**, not the text. **Do not claim a Glagolitic inscription naming the name until Fučić's own entry is read.**

**What it gives instead is worth more.** **Gologorica was writing Glagolitic from at least 1549**, and this family arrived into it and in **1711** cut **arms, a Latin inscription and a relief of Christ** over a door the encyclopaedia calls *«a modest palace of village landowners»*. **That is their social position, in one sentence, on the house itself.**

rows.what: Uršula Kovačina's own family, found in the Crikvenica marriages of 1895
rows.note:
**Reading the marriage film for a Defranceschi produced a Kovačina instead.** Crikvenica marriages **1895, entry 28, 28 November**: **«Petar Kovačina, stolar»** — a joiner — marries **«Marija Car»**, at **Crikvenica house 119**. His father is another **Petar Kovačina**.

**Uršula Kovačina married Anton Rudolf Defranceschi** and is David's great-grandmother; she was born at Crikvenica about 1890–95 and died at Belgrade in 1975. Until now her family existed in this archive **only as a surname on a tree**. Here is a Kovačina household in a register, with a trade and a house number.

**What to do, and it is already half-ordered:** the **Crikvenica birth register 1890–1896** — wanted on [the errands](/errands/) for the modern households anyway — would show whether Uršula is a daughter of this house, and would give her parents outright. House **119** is the thread to pull.

*inf — a Kovačina at Crikvenica in 1895 is very likely her kin; which kin is exactly what is not yet known.*

---

**Done, 20 September 2026 — and it closed a question this archive had deliberately left open.**

The **Crikvenica marriage of 28 November 1895** gives the groom's parents in full: **«Petar Kovačina, k. r. financ. nadstražar, i Uršula rodj. Stojčić»** — the very two people the 1904 death entry names. **Petar Kovačina the joiner is the son of Petar Kovačina the financial guard**, not a brother and not the same man under an earlier trade.

Three generations of house 119 now stand: **the guard and Uršula née Stojčić → the joiner and Marija Car (m. 1895, by leave of the Royal Hungarian ministry) → Uršula, who married Anton Rudolf.**

**What is still inference:** that Anton Rudolf's wife is the joiner's daughter. **Next: Crikvenica births 1896–1902 for a Uršula Kovačina at house 119.**

rows.what: Anna Kalanj's brother is named — now get the whole Ledenice household
rows.note:
**Found on 20 September in the Crikvenica marriages, 1899 entry 12**: *«Josip Kalanj, zidar, iz Ledenica»*, of **Ledenice house 37**, son of **Josip Kalanj and Rosalija née Perković**, marrying **Marija Poštrenčić**, a seamstress. **Those are Anna Kalanj's parents**, from her own Ledenice baptism of 1864 — so this is **her brother**, and **Anton Rudolf's maternal uncle**.

**It is the first time the bride's side of the Klenovica marriage has been in a register at all**, and it says what they did: **masons**.

**Three things follow, and all are in Ledenice:**

· the **Ledenice births, about 1860–1875**, should hold **Anna and her brothers in one household** — the whole sibling set this archive has never had;
· the **Ledenice marriages after 1882** are the volume that would hold **Anna's own marriage to Josip Defranceschi**, and they are **not on the film this archive has been reading** — they must be asked for from the Matični ured;
· **Luka Kalanj, son of Martin, mason**, stood witness, and **Ivan Kalanj** married in the same register three weeks earlier to *different* parents. **There is more than one Kalanj household**, and telling them apart is what the Ledenice births would do.

*This is the film paying for itself in a way that was not the plan: it does not hold the Defranceschi marriage, but it has handed over the bride's family.*

---

**Done, 20 September 2026 — and it answered more than it asked.**

**Anna Kalanj is the third of eight children** of Josip Kalanj and Rosalija née Perković: **Thomas 1858 · Martinus 1861 · ANNA 1864 · Lucia 1866 · Franciscus 1868 · Josephus 1871 · Maria 1874 · Joannes 1877.** The FamilySearch index located the pages; **each entry was then read on the register image**.

**Josephus, born 5 May 1871, is the «Josip Kalanj, zidar» who married at Crikvenica in 1899** — so the brother found from the marriage and the brother found from the baptisms are the same man, confirmed from both ends.

**And the house is the find.** The clerk writes it as **«Ledenice in Klenovica N° 22»** (1861), **«Rljinovica N° 22»** (1864), **«Ledenice N° 22 in Rljenovice»** (1866) and **«Povile N° 22»** (1871, 1877). **Anton Rudolf was born at «Klenovica kbr. 22» in 1890 — the same house.** *See item 76.*

rows.what: Read the Bribir marriage register 1858–1900 — the last filmed Vinodol marriage book that could hold Josip and Ana
rows.note:
**Bribir, Vjenčani 1858–1900** (waypoint `9R28-L2Q:391644801,391644802,391654901`) covers the whole window in which the marriage of **Josip Defranceschi × Anna Kalanj** must fall, and this archive's earlier shelf survey wrongly recorded Bribir's marriages as stopping in 1858.

**It is now the only filmed Vinodol marriage register left unread.** Crikvenica 1859–1908 is read end to end and clean; Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica 1859–1910 is read across 1882–1891 and clean; Ledenice stops at 1882 and Novi Vinodolski at 1859.

*The method is settled: the left page of these Austrian tabular registers carries both spouses, their origin and their domicile, so one crop a page finds the surname.*

---

**Done, 20 September 2026. Bribir is read and clean.**

**1883–1890 complete — about four hundred marriages — and no Defranceschi in any of them.** Year totals off the priest's own numbering: **1883: 57 · 1884: 45 · 1885: 64 · 1886: 41 · 1887: 45 · 1888: 25 · 1889: 22 · 1890: 24.**

**A catalogue trap worth knowing:** the waypoint for *Vjenčani 1858–1900* returns **597 images**, because Bribir's births, marriages and deaths share one reel. The **marriages sit around images 108–150**; everything past about 250 is the death register.

**With this, every filmed Vinodol marriage register covering 1883–1889 has been read and every one is negative** — Crikvenica 1859–1908, Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica 1859–1910, and now Bribir. Ledenice stops at 1882 and Novi Vinodolski at 1859. *There is nothing left on film. What remains is the letter to Rijeka — item 141.*

rows.what: Ask Rijeka for the Klenovica and Ledenice marriage registers after 1882 — the books the films do not reach
rows.note:
**This is now the likeliest home of the marriage, and it cannot be read from a screen.**

Anton Rudolf's baptism of 20 January 1890 is in a **Klenovica** register catalogued as **«Matične knjige, Ledenice / Klenovica»**, and its remarks column says the parents were at Klenovica only because they were **staying with Ana's parents** — *«kod roditelja žene Ane»* — at **house 22**, where the godfather **Jakov Kalanj** also lived. **Klenovica is the bride's family's village.** Marriages are normally celebrated in the bride's parish.

**Neither book is on FamilySearch.** Klenovica does not exist as a parish in the FamilySearch tree at all; Ledenice's marriage film stops at **1882**. So the two registers most likely to hold this marriage — **Klenovica's own marriage book** and **Ledenice's marriages after 1882** — have to be asked for.

**Where to ask:** the **Državni arhiv u Rijeci** holds the Vinodol parish books (Crikvenica's own volume is theirs: *Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4), inv. 110*), and the **Matični ured** for Novi Vinodolski holds what the archive has not taken in. **Ask for the marriage register of Klenovica and of Ledenice covering 1883–1890, and for any entry for Josip Defranceschi and Ana Kalanj in either.**

*This is David's letter to send, not a film to read.*

**20 Sept 2026 — a second thing to ask for in the same letter.** The Crikvenica **births** for **1897–1902** are wanted too, for **Uršula Kovačina**, daughter of Petar Kovačina *stolar* and Marija Car of **house 119** — Anton Rudolf's wife. The whole of filmed 1896 has now been read entry by entry and she is not in it, the FamilySearch index holds no Uršula Kovačina birth anywhere in Croatia, and **the parish's birth register is not filmed past 1896**. Her parents married in November 1895 and a sister was born about March 1897, so she falls squarely in the unfilmed years. **Until that register is read, the line from the financial guard's son to Anton Rudolf's wife is inference and nothing more.**

rows.what: Is Giuseppe × Francesca of Fiume a sixteenth child of Valentino the Carnian?
rows.note:
**This is the join that would matter most, and it is one register away.**

The index sweep of 20 September turned up a **four-generation chain at Rijeka**: **Giuseppe Defranceschi × Francesca** → **Valentino b. 1772**, who fathers **twenty-one indexed children** on Ursula between 1794 and 1805 → **Franciscus b. 1797**, who fathers four more to 1836.

**The archive's own Fiume household is Valentino the Carnian**, citizen of 1739, fifteen children 1737–1757. A Giuseppe whose son is christened **Valentino** about 1772, in the same town, is what a grandson looks like — **but there is no Giuseppe among the fifteen.**

**Why that is not fatal.** The fifteen were **fourteen until 20 September**, when Jacobus Vincentius was found in the index and then read on the page. The 6 September reading covered the dates it was given, not the whole book.

**What settles it.** The **Fiume St Vitus baptisms for 1758–1775**, on **film 005497925** — the same film already anchored for this archive, where **image 293 is 21 July 1757** and the volume runs on. A Giuseppe born to Valentino and Helena after 1757 would close the gap; his absence over eighteen years would open it. Either way it is a bounded read of one film at known frames.

**If it joins, it joins a lot.** The Rijeka family of 1794–1805 is twenty-one children this archive has never attached to anything, and they would hang off the Carnian household directly.

**Narrowed the same day, and the window is now five years wide.**

**The far end is dated.** The index carries **«Valentinum Josephum Gregorium Defranceschi, f. **Josephi**, m. **Francæ**, 11/12 March 1776, Vitipolis»** — so Giuseppe × Franca were baptising at Fiume in 1776, and their son is the Valentino who fathers the twenty-one.

**Which dates Giuseppe himself.** A man with a son born in 1776 was born by about 1750 — **inside** Valentino the Carnian's childbearing window, not after it. So the question is not «is there a sixteenth child after 1757» but **«is there one in the gaps»**.

**And the fifteen have gaps.** They fall in 1737, 1739, 1741, 1742×3, 1745, 1751, 1752, 1753, 1754, 1755 and 1757×3. The holes are **1743–44, 1746–50 and 1756** — and **1746–1750 is a five-year silence** in a household that otherwise produces a child every year or two. **That is where a Giuseppe would be.**

**The read, precisely.** Film **005497925**. Ignatius was found at **image 126 = 29 July 1745** and Vitus at **image 228 = 18 June 1751**, so 1746–1750 lies between them — roughly **95 frames**, both pages each. *⚠ The frame arithmetic across that span is not safe*: images 126 and 228 sit under **different waypoints** (`9R2X-ZNT…714201` and `9R2X-C62…714501`), and image 203 of the first shows a year in the 1780s, so the two are not one continuous sequence. **Anchor by reading, not by interpolating across the join.**

**The index cannot do it.** A sweep of 2,251 rows finds **no Giuseppe with a Valentin- father anywhere**, and four of the fifteen children were already known to be in no index at all. **Absence in the index is not absence in the book** — this item exists because that has already been proved twice on this film.

**Scoped properly, and the earlier warning on this item was wrong.**

This item said the two ends of the read sat under different waypoints and that image 203 of the first showed a year in the 1780s, so the frames could not be interpolated across. **That was a misreading of image 203.** Probing the volume directly shows it is **continuous**:

| film image | date |
|---|---|
| 126 | 29 July **1745** — Ignatius |
| 135 | 10–11 July **1746** |
| 153 | 7–9 September **1748** |
| 171 | **marriages, 1738** — the baptism run has ended |

So volume one runs at **about 8.3 frames to the year**, and its **baptisms stop before image 171**, where a marriage register begins on the same reel. **The window is images 127–170 — forty-four frames, not ninety-five**, and there is no unsafe join inside it.

**The index will not do it.** There are **no indexed Defranceschi baptisms at Fiume at all between 1746 and 1750** — but that discriminates nothing, because **three of the children already known from this stretch (Ignatius 1745, Vitus 1751, Rosalia 1755) are in no index either**. Silence in the index is this film's normal state for this family.

**Ready to run:** forty-four frames, both pages, looking for *«Valentini»* in the father's slot. The arks are in `scratchpad/fiume/arks.lst`, lines 127–170.

**20 Sept, later — one page beat the forty-four.** Giuseppe × Francesca have **four children indexed at Fiume** (1772, 1774, 1776, 1778). The eldest son's entry, **23 November 1772**, reads *«Valentinus Franciscus Xaverius, filius legitimus **DD. Josephi, et Franciscæ jugalium Defranceschi**, heri natus, baptizavit C.us Lumaga, Levantibus D.no Francisco Tomassich **et D.na Helena Defranceschi**»*.

**Valentino the Carnian's wife was Helena**, and in 1772 she would be in her mid-fifties. **A Helena Defranceschi at the font for Giuseppe's first son is a grandmother.** The celebrant, **Canonicus Lumaga**, is the same name as the canon who baptised Valentino's own son Aloysius Rochus in 1754.

*Still inf — another Helena Defranceschi at Fiume is possible.* **The 1746–1750 read (images 127–170) would settle it outright** and remains the way to close this item.

**20 Sept, later still — the scoping above is wrong and the volumes are now mapped properly.** Each waypoint on this reel is a **bound volume holding births and marriages together**, with different date ranges: `9R2X-ZNT` = births **1734–1749** + marriages **1734–1753**; `9R2X-C62` = births **1749–1769** + marriages **1753–1776**. So *«forty-four frames, images 127–170»* was wrong twice over — volume one's **births stop at 1749**, and images 171+ are **marriages of 1738**. Image 203 is **1753**, not the 1780s; that misreading has now been made twice and is retired.

**Baptisms read so far:** volume 1 images **127–133**, both pages, **August 1745 to May 1746**. No Defranceschi as father. Incidentally **Helena Defranceschi stands godmother four times** in those seven frames, and a **Catharina Defranceschi** once — who cannot be Josepha Catharina b. 1737, aged eight. *A Defranceschi woman not yet in this archive.*

**Marriages read:** volume 2 images **286, 291, 292, 293** — March 1769 to December 1771. **No Giuseppe.** But 293R gives **Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, widower, marrying Catharina de Benzoni on 9 December 1771**.

**Next, and cheapest first:** volume 2 images **294–304** (marriages 1772–1776) for Giuseppe's own wedding, which would name his father outright. Then volume 1 images **134–170** and volume 2's early births for the 1746–1749 baptism gap.

**Marriage sweep done, and it is a nil that redirects the item.** Both pages of images **286, 289–295** of volume 2 — **1769 through August 1772** — hold **no Giuseppe Defranceschi marriage**. Since he baptises his first child at Fiume on 23 November 1772, **he married outside the town, almost certainly in Francesca's parish.** **The entry that names his father exists; it is somewhere else, and the way to it is to identify Francesca.** Images 287–288 (about June–November 1769) are the only gap left in the Fiume run.

*And a caution on the Benzoni:* they witness unrelated gentry marriages on image 289 too, so their appearance around Valentino's children in 1754–55 is **not** a family marker and should not be leaned on.

**Baptism sweep tally.** Both pages of images **127–134, 136, 137** now read — **22 August 1745 to 2 October 1746**. **No Defranceschi as a father in any of it.** Unread: **138–170** (Oct 1746 to 1749) and the second gap at images **~104–125** (1743–44).

**And the four children of Giuseppe × Francesca now have arks**, so whoever picks this up can go straight to them: **1772** `3QS7-899F-WCFK` *(read — Helena Defranceschi godmother)*; **1774** `3QS7-899F-WHG6`; **1776** `3QS7-899F-WC34`; **1778** `3QSQ-G99F-WHGT` *(located on the page — «Die 8 Feb. 1778. Hellenam Ludovicam filiam legitimam D.ni Josephi et…» — godparent line not yet magnified)*. **Their godparents are the cheapest remaining lead**: a Defranceschi sibling standing for one of them would name the household without needing the 1746–49 grind.

**The godparent read paid, and it is the best evidence this item has.** Giuseppe's second child, **12 July 1774** (`3QS7-899F-WHG6`): *«Hellenam Margaritham Mariam filiam legitimam D.D. Josephi et Franciscæ jugalium Defranceschi… levantibus **D.no Ignatio Defranceschi** et D.na Theresia Tomasich»*.

**Ignatius Francus Mattheus is one of Valentino's fifteen**, baptised 29 July 1745 on image 126 of this same film — one of the four in no index at all. In 1774 he is twenty-eight. **So Valentino's wife stands for Giuseppe's first child (1772) and Valentino's son for his second (1774).** The forename is rare and this archive knows no other Ignatius Defranceschi at Fiume.

*Still short of proof — no entry says «Josephus filius Valentini».* **Remaining: the 1776 baptism (`3QS7-899F-WC34`) and the 1778 godparent line (`3QSQ-G99F-WHGT`), then the 1746–1749 gap or a death entry giving Giuseppe's age and father.**

**All four godparent sets now read.** **1772** Helena Defranceschi · **1774 Ignatio Defranceschi** · **1776 Carolo Müller and Josepha Callinesi — no Defranceschi** · **1778 Ludovico Henrich and Hellena Carina — no Defranceschi** (resolved on a fifth crop; *Carina* also witnessed the Defranceschi–Benzoni marriage of 1771). **So: two of four, settled**, and settled against the reading this archive wanted. Fiume godparents were as much patronage as kin.

**20 Sept, the sweep resumed — and the recurring Helena now has a name.** Both pages of images **138–140** read: **10 November 1746 to 17 February 1747**, no Defranceschi father. The running total of volume 1 baptisms read is now **127–134, 136–140** — *22 August 1745 to 17 February 1747*.

On **140R, 26 January 1747**, «patrini fuerunt D.nus Cosar, **et Helena Defranceschi**» — her **fifth** appearance in fourteen frames. **Valentino the Carnian's wife was Helena**, and she is the only Helena Defranceschi known to be living at Fiume then, so the recurring godmother is almost certainly her. She is written **plain** in 1747 and **D.na** in 1772, matching the household's own rise from *Valentinus* to *D.nus Valentinus* in the 1750s.

**This cuts both ways and the cut against is the important one.** Five appearances in fourteen frames make her a **habitual** godmother, so her presence at Giuseppe's first son in 1772 is weak evidence of kinship — weaker than this item once claimed. **Ignatio in 1774 is the load-bearing one**, being a single appearance of a rare forename. *And a rival Helena exists*: b. 1725, d. 1809, of **Gologorica** — right age, wrong town. The entries give no patronymic, so the identification is by residence only. **inf.**

**Death route closed for now.** The index carries **no burial for our Giuseppe** — 36 rows of the forename, one death-typed, and that man was **born 1784**. A death entry would give his age and probably his father, so it remains the best single document; it just has to be **browsed**, in Fiume **Deaths 1766–1815** (`9R26-YWL`).

**Unread on the gap:** volume 1 images **141–170** (Feb 1747 to 1749) and volume 2's early births for 1749; plus the second gap at images **~104–125** (1743–44).

**20 Sept — the gap gave up a child, and it is not the one this item wanted.** Images **138–146** of volume 1 now read, both pages: **10 November 1746 to 16 October 1747**, continuous. On **image 146L**, under «Die 13 8bris 1747»:

> «Franciscam Matthæam filiam legitimam D.ni **Valentini**, et **Helenæ** jugalium **Defranceschi**, natam 10 hujus, baptizavit D.nus Canonicus Hieronymus Moroldo.»

**A sixteenth child — a daughter, born 10 October 1747, in no index anywhere.** She is not Matheus Franciscus, who is 1739 and has his own ark.

**This retires the premise of this item and sharpens it at the same time.** The «five-year silence of 1746–1750» was the reason to think a hidden Giuseppe was plausible. **There was no silence** — the household was baptising in 1747, and the archive simply had not read the page. So the argument from absence is gone. But the same fact says the gap is **productive**: the first nine frames swept produced a Defranceschi baptism, and **images 147–170 and ~104–125 are still unread**. If a Giuseppe exists, that is where he is, and he will be found by reading rather than by inference.

**A correction has been published** for the «fifteen children» heading, for the five-year-silence claim, and for dating the household's *D.nus / Ill.mus* styling to «the 1750s» — the 1747 entry already carries both.

**Helena's tally is now eight**: four in images 127–133, then 26 January, 26 February, 26 March and 30 July 1747. That is a parish godmother, and it is the reason her 1772 appearance at Giuseppe's son carries little weight on its own.

**20 Sept — answered, and not in the direction this item was pointing.** Image **150R** of volume 1:

> «Die 29 May 1748. **Josephum Aloysium** filium legitimum D.ni **Joannis Baptæ** et D.næ **Magdalenæ** jugalium **de Franceschi**, natum 24 hujus, baptizavit D.nus Canonicus Eustachius Sauf. Patrini fuere D.nus Josephus Voxila et D.na Eleonora Franul.»

**Giuseppe was born on 24 May 1748, and his father was Joannes Baptista, not Valentino.**

The identification rests on five things that agree: the **forename**, the **surname**, the **town**, an **age of 24** at his first child's baptism in November 1772 — and the fact that this archive had already found **«Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, widower»** marrying **Catharina de Benzoni on 9 December 1771**, which is exactly the status of a man whose wife *Magdalena* had died. The MyHeritage tree's unsourced **b. 1748, d. 1778** for Giuseppe now has a document behind the birth year, and the death year sits in the same year as his last child's baptism.

*Still inf:* **no entry says «Josephus filius Joannis Baptistæ»**. But this is far stronger than the godparent argument, and it is the first document that gives Giuseppe a father at all.

**So the answer to the question as asked is: no.** Giuseppe is **not** a sixteenth child of Valentino. He belongs to a **second Defranceschi household** at Fiume, and **Helena in 1772 and Ignatio in 1774 were the other household standing for its kin** — which was always the better reading of a habitual godmother.

**Marking this done and opening the question it leaves.** How **Joannes Baptista** and **Valentino** are related is now the join that matters, and it is answerable: their marriage entries are on **this same reel**, in volume 1's **marriages of 1734–1753**, and a marriage entry names a father and usually a birthplace. That is item **143**.

rows.what: How are Joannes Baptista and Valentino Defranceschi of Fiume related?
rows.note:
**Two Defranceschi households baptised at Fiume in the 1740s, and nothing yet connects them.**

**Valentino × Helena** — *«venuto dalla Carnia»*, citizen of Fiume in 1739, **sixteen children 1737–1757**.

**Joannes Baptista × Magdalena** — styled *D.nus*, baptising **Josephus Aloysius on 29 May 1748** (film 005497925, image 150). A **widower by 9 December 1771**, when he marries **Catharina de Benzoni** (volume 2, image 293), with indexed children by her in **1773** and **1776**. **Josephus Aloysius is almost certainly the Giuseppe who heads the Rijeka chain**, which makes this household the trunk of twenty-six indexed descendants, not a footnote.

**He is not Valentino's son.** The only *Joannes Baptista* among Valentino's sixteen was baptised in **1751** and cannot father a child in 1748. Brother, cousin, or no relation at all — the register has not said.

**Why it is worth a name:** if they are brothers, the Rijeka chain hangs off **Carnia** and joins the Mione line this archive already holds. If they are not, Fiume held two unrelated families of the name and a great deal of this archive's Kvarner material has been read as one thing when it is two.

**The read, precisely.** **Film 005497925, volume 1**, which carries **marriages 1734–1753** from about **image 171** — image 171 is already known to show marriages of 1738. **Joannes Baptista × Magdalena must marry before May 1748**, so the window is **1734–1748**, and **Valentino × Helena marry before November 1737**, so they are in the same run or just before it. A Fiume marriage entry names **the father of each party** and usually **where he is from**. **Two entries would settle it.**

*Cheaper still if it works:* volume 2 carries **marriages 1753–1776**, already partly read for 1769–1772. Nothing there bears on this, so the read is volume 1's marriage section and nothing else.

**20 Sept — one of the two marriages is found.** Walking the marriage run backwards from image 189 (*October 1746*) through 170 and 169 to **168R**, second entry:

> «Die 28 Februarij 1737. D.num **Valentinum de Franceschi ex Carnia**, et **Elenam Surcho** junxit in matrimonium D.nus Petrus Eustachius Sauss Canonicus, præsentibus testibus Nob. D.no Petro Petrini et Nob. D.no Antonio Moretti.»

**«Ex Carnia» is now primary**, two years before the citizenship of 1739, and Valentino's wife has a maiden name for the first time: **Elena Surcho**. *(Initial S or Z; given as read.)*

**But the entry names no father** — Fiume marriage entries of this decade give the celebrant and the witnesses and stop there. So **this join will not be made by filiation**. It will be made, if at all, by **finding Joannes Baptista × Magdalena in the same run and seeing whether the clerk writes «ex Carnia» over him too** — and, better, by whether their witnesses are the same men.

**Read so far:** images **168, 169, 170, 189**. **Unread: 171–188** (1738–1746) and **190–205** (1747–1753). Joannes Baptista must marry **before May 1748**, so **171–190** is the window, and it is **twenty frames**.

**20 Sept — the Fiume marriage run is now read end to end, and the answer is a nil that moves the item.** **Images 168–191, both pages, November 1736 to February 1748.** In twelve years there is **one Defranceschi marriage**: Valentino's own. **Joannes Baptista × Magdalena are not in it.**

Their son was born **24 May 1748**, so if they had married at Fiume they would be inside that window. **They married somewhere else** — exactly as their son Giuseppe would, and exactly as an incomer does.

**So this item leaves Fiume.** Kobler's claim is that a **Giovanni Battista De Franceschi came to Fiume from the Contea di Pisino intorno al 1740** and was *«senz'altro»* of the Gologorica family — **this archive's own line**. His pedigree adds that the man **studied at Fiume** and **married a lady of the D'Agnese family**.

**The test is now a single fact: Magdalena's maiden name.** *D'Agnese confirms Kobler and hangs the whole Rijeka chain off this archive's own line. Anything else kills it.* And the place to find it is **the County of Pazin's registers, which run from 1582 and this archive has never opened**, not Fiume.

**Incidental, and worth having:** Valentino stands **witness** at a Fiume wedding on **28 February 1740** (image 175L), three years to the day after his own — an occurrence in no index. And a **near-miss is retired**: *«Perill.ri D.no Josepho **Defranchi**»*, witness on image 187R in December 1745, is **de Franchi**, a different surname.

**20 Sept, scoped — and the shelf is shorter than the question.** Of the collection's 43 Istrian parishes, only **two** in the County of Pazin have marriage books covering **1740–1748**: **Pazin** (1656–1852) and **Tinjan** (1703–1896). **Gologorica, Gračišće, Pićan and Žminj are not in the collection at all** — and Gologorica is the house with 1711 over the door.

**So a nil at Pazin and Tinjan does not disprove Kobler.** It would mean the entry is in a book that cannot be opened from here, which is an errand, not a read. *Do not let a negative close this item.*

**Tinjan first.** Darovec, quoted on this site already, puts the Friulian-Carnian stratum in *«Pazin, Pićan, Gradišće, Žminj and Tinjan»* — and Tinjan is the only one of the five that is filmed.

**Pazin is enumerated and anchored, ready to run:** waypoint `9R26-16F:391644801,392372801,392373301`, **396 frames**, arks saved to `scratchpad/pazin/arks.lst`. **Index 134 = January 1741. Index 142 = 1746. Index 160 = October 1747 – January 1748.** **Read frames 128–165.** *The volume binds three date-runs together, so anchor by reading and never by interpolating across them.*

**20 Sept — Tinjan read, and it is a nil.** **Marriages 1703–1896**, frames **9–13**, both pages: **1733–1735 and 1741–1749**. **No form of the surname anywhere** — not groom, bride, father or witness. The grooms are Červar, Milinarić, Antolović, Šubić, Smokovac, Dobrila: **a Croatian village marrying its own**, with Italian names appearing only as the notaries who witness everything.

*That is worth having:* it says an incoming Carnian family is **not** quietly marrying into Tinjan in these years, which the Darovec quotation might have led this archive to assume.

**Gap: 1736–1740 was not located.** Frame 9 ends 1735, frame 10 opens «Conjuncti sub Par.o Joanne… 1741». The volume already runs out of order, so those years may be elsewhere in it. **A marriage up to 1747 is covered; 1736–1740 is not.**

**Still open, in order:** Tinjan **1736–1740** if it exists in the volume; then **Pazin marriages, frames 128–165** (arks in `scratchpad/pazin/arks.lst`). **And neither can close this item**, because Gologorica, Gračišće, Pićan and Žminj are not filmed here — reaching those is an **errand**, not a read.

**⚠ 20 Sept, later — the Pazin frame window published above is WRONG. Do not use it.** The years read as **1741 / 1746 / 1747** at frames 134 / 142 / 160 are **1711 / 1716 / 1717**: this clerk's **4** and **1** are not distinguishable at page scale. **Frame 143 writes 1717 twice cleanly**, which cannot sit eight frames after 1746.

**Re-anchored, all read:** **143 = 1717**, **178 = 1733**, **198 = 1742**, **200 = blank leaf**, **205 = a microfilm resolution target**, i.e. a volume boundary. **≈ 2.2 frames to the year.**

**The window for 1740–1748 is frames ≈194–204**, and it runs into the boundary at 205 — so check whether the last years continue in the section after the target. **Eleven frames and a join.** Arks 175–234 are in `scratchpad/pazin/arks175.lst`; 0–179 in `arks.lst`.

*A correction is published for this. When anchoring by date heading in this hand, cross-check every year against a neighbouring frame — and check that the run is possible before writing it down.*

**20 Sept — Pazin read end to end, and it is a nil. The online shelf for this question is exhausted.**

**Frames 194–199 (Dec 1740 – Nov 1742) and 208–216 (1743 – Nov 1748)**, both pages each. **No form of the surname in any role.** The couples are Sgrablich, Mattesich, Cerovaz, Brattulich, Sironich, Mogorovich — an Istrian town marrying its own — and the Italian and German names belong to the Praepositus and the chaplain who officiate.

**The volume is three filmed items on one reel.** The 1656– run **stops at November 1742** on carta 150, then blank leaves, an **«END OF ITEM»** card at 203 and a resolution target at 205, and **resumes at 1743** in the next item. Interpolating across that join lands in the wrong decade.

**Both filmed parishes of the Contea di Pisino are now nil for the window** — Tinjan 1741–1749, Pazin 1740–1748. **And neither touches Kobler**, because Gologorica, Gračišće, Pićan and Žminj are in no part of this collection.

**This item is now an errand, not a read.** What would answer it is the **Državni arhiv u Pazinu**, which holds the books themselves. *Leave the item open; do not close it on these nils.*

---

**21 September 2026 — out of reach of full-text search, measured.** FamilySearch full-text indexes **Italian civil registration**, not the Croatia Church Books: 97 collections sampled from its own results carry **zero** Croatian entries. This item is a Croatian church register and **no query will reach it**. It stays an archive question.

---

**21 September 2026 — the premise is in doubt.** FamilySearch's own household index for **image 150** reads the 29 May 1748 baptism as **«Josephum Aloysium MANCOSCHI», parents «Joannis Bapte Mancoschi» and «Magdalená Mancoschi»** — the same date, the same child's forenames and the same parents' forenames this archive records as **Defranceschi**, with a different surname. Either the index misread *de Franceschi*, or this household was never ours and **there is no second Fiume house to relate Valentino's to**. **The plate has not been magnified** and until it is, this item cannot be answered — it can only be asked more precisely. See [/searched/](/searched/).

**21 September 2026, later — SETTLED, and the premise holds.** The plate reads *«Josephum Aloysium filium legitimum D.ni Joannis Baptæ et D.næ Magdalenæ jugalium **DE FRANCESCHI**, natus 28 hujus»*. **The index's «Mancoschi» is simply wrong.** There are two Defranceschi households at Fiume in the 1740s and the question of how they relate is live again. **The godparents are Josephus Voxila and Eleonora Frauel — neither a Defranceschi — so this entry does not itself join the two houses.** The next move is the same treatment on Valentino's sixteen baptisms, looking for a Defranceschi in anyone's godparent line.

**21 September 2026, third pass — the first of Valentino's baptisms read on the plate.** **17 September 1739**: *«Matthæus Franciscus filius legitimus **D. Valentini et Helenæ jugalium Defranceschi**… Patrini fuere **Nob. D.nus Petrus Ronaldi**, et **Nob. D.na Margarita uxor D.ni Georgij Vlah, Capitanei Cast[u]anensis**»*. **No Defranceschi godparent** — so this entry does not join the houses either, and that is now two baptisms read with the same negative.

**What it does give is the social register.** Valentino is styled ***D.*** in the very year he became a citizen of Fiume, and his son's godparents are **nobles**, one of them the wife of the **Captain of Kastav**. Joannes Baptista's household is likewise *D.ni* with *D.nus/D.na* godparents. **Two Defranceschi houses in one port, both addressed as gentry, in one decade** — a shared milieu, not yet a shared descent. **Next: the remaining baptisms of Valentino × Helena, same treatment.**

**21 September 2026, fourth pass — four baptisms read, and the negative is now solid.** 17 Sep 1739, 4 Sep 1741, 29 May 1748 and 26 Jun 1752, all read off the plate. **Not one Defranceschi among the eight godparents.** Every one of the eight carries an honorific — four are *Nobilis* — including the wife of the **Captain of Kastav** and the noble widow **Antonia Monaldi**, who stands for other families on the same leaf. **Both households move among the port's nobility; no thread yet joins them to each other.** *Vitipolis*, the index's place for Valentino's children, is very probably **Fiume** itself — *Terra Fluminis Sancti Viti*, the city of St Vitus — which removes the apparent contradiction with the film. *(inf.)*

**22 September 2026 — fifth baptism read, same answer.** 19 December 1742, *Francisca Joanna Theresia*, godparents **D. Antonius de Campo Xenes** and **Nob. D.na Vidua Margaritha Salopp**. **Five baptisms, ten godparents, no Defranceschi.** Also settled: *Mattio* and *Antonio*, held here as children born 1742 and 1753, are **burials** — so Valentino and Helena lost a child in July 1742 and an infant in September 1753. **The godparent route is close to exhausted; the marriage registers are the next place to look.**

**22 September 2026 — the marriage route tested and the index is empty.** Exact-surname *Franceschi* marriages across Croatia 1715–1775 return **120**, filtered to Fiume **62**, and **neither Fiume marriage is among them**. Most of the 62 are **Omiš**; two that looked like our couple are 1846 and 1852 **Masatto** marriages where *Franceschi* is a mother's maiden name; one genuine 1738 marriage (*Antonio × Margaritta Cambi*) sits on **film 005494172**, not Fiume's, with no place given.

**This item is not answerable from an index**, and that is now shown rather than supposed. The route is **the Fiume marriage register read on the plate**. **And the possibility that the answer is «they are not related» should stay open** — five baptisms with no Defranceschi godparent is the shape unrelated households make.

**22 September 2026 — the marriage register is open, and it was never a separate film.** The volume is **«Births 1734–1749 · Marriages 1734–1753», Rijeka** — one book, filmed as **005497925**, baptisms to about image 155 and **marriages in the back fifty frames**. This archive had been treating the film as a baptism register.

**Frame 175, 28 February 1740**: *«…in matrimonium conjunxit D.nus Canonicus Devicho, **præsentibus testibus D.no Valentino Defranceschi**, et D.no Gregorio Kesner»*. **Valentino stands witness at a Fiume wedding**, styled *D.no*, four months after becoming a citizen. The next entry on the same leaf is witnessed by **Nob. D. Antonio Spingarolli**, godfather to Valentino's son in 1741. **Defranceschi, Spingarolli and Monaldi recur together across both registers.**

**Still to read: the remaining fifty frames.** A marriage of either Fiume man would name his parents outright, which is the one thing that would settle this item either way.

---

**22 September 2026 — the front of the marriage volume is closed, and the «remaining fifty frames» line was stale.**

**Frames 160–167, both pages: 1 January 1734 to November 1736. No Defranceschi in any role** — not groom, bride or witness.

**The volume has a beginning, and this is it.** Frame **160 left** is a blank leaf; frame **160 right** carries the heading ***«Liber Matrimoniorum Anni 1734. Sit Laus Deo, ac B. Virgini Mariæ»*** on book page **150**, with the first entry dated **1 January 1734**. Frames **155–159** are the tail of the *baptism* volume, still in **1749** — the two registers sit back to back in one book, and the marriage section runs **160 → 1734** onward while the baptisms run to 1749, so the film's date order reverses at frame 160.

**What that settles:** Valentino's wedding of **28 February 1737** is the **first Defranceschi marriage in the book**, with nothing of the name before it. Read together with the 20 September sweep of **168–191**, the surname appears **once** in fourteen years of Fiume weddings, 1734–1748.
