**And the reading of his own entry is corrected in one place.** The second witness, published here as *«Nob. D.no Antonio **Moretti**»*, is **Nob. D.no Antonio MONALDI** — magnified and set beside a securely-read *«Laurentius Monaldi»* two frames earlier in the same hand, where the looped **ld** ligature is identical and the double **t** of *Moretti* is simply not on the page. **So Valentino's own wedding is witnessed by a Monaldi**, on the day he married, in the parish the Monaldi archpriest ran — the earliest link in the **Defranceschi–Spingarolli–Monaldi** circle by two years. *(The archpriest **Petrus Maria Monaldi** died in the autumn of 1736; a marginal note on frame 167 records the parish vacant until 4 March 1737 and a new parish priest installed 29 September 1737, which is why a canon and not the archpriest marries Valentino.)*

**The bride's surname gains a third live reading.** The initial is this hand's ambiguous looped capital, so *Surcho* and *Zurcho* stand — but the body of the word is plainly **-urcho**, and **Turcho** belongs on the list beside them, because *Turco / Turcho* is a common name on this coast and *Surcho* is not. *Given as read; no one of the three is preferred.*

**Unread is not fifty frames, it is the tail.** **168–191 were read on 20 September**; the note above asking for «the remaining fifty frames» was written without that sweep in view. What is genuinely unread is **192 onward** — frame **200** is **1751**, and the volume's marriages end in **1753**. *That stretch is after Joannes Baptista's son was born, so it cannot hold his marriage; it is worth reading for any other Defranceschi, and for whether he appears as a witness.*

---

**22 September 2026, later — the Fiume marriage volume is read END TO END, and the count is one.**

**Frames 160–204. 1 January 1734 to 7 February 1753. Nineteen years, both pages of every frame.** Frame **204 right is a blank leaf** (book page 194) and frame **205 is the microfilm's «END OF ITEM» card**, so the volume has a documented back cover as well as a documented title page.

**In nineteen years of Fiume weddings the surname appears once: Valentino's, 28 February 1737.** Not as a groom, not as a bride, not as a witness — with the single exception already known, Valentino standing witness on 28 February 1740.

**The tail read today, 192–204, is Joannes Baptista's last chance and he is not in it either.** June 1748 to February 1753, the years *after* his son's birth. He does not marry at Fiume before 1748 and he does not marry at Fiume after it; his Fiume marriage is to **Catharina de Benzoni in 1771**, in volume 2, as a **widower**. *Magdalena was married somewhere else, and this volume can no longer be asked about her.*

**The join between the two sweeps was tested, not assumed.** Frame 191 ends on **25 February 1748** and frame 192 opens on **2 June 1748** — a three-month hole exactly where two sessions' work meets, which is the most dangerous place on a reel. **It is not a missing leaf.** The pencil foliation runs **181 → 182** unbroken across the two frames, and **Ash Wednesday 1748 fell on 28 February**: the last wedding is three days before Lent begins and the register resumes after it. *The gap is the closed season, and the book is whole.* [Logged as method](/method/).

**One caution on the Monaldi correction above.** *Moretti* is **not** absent from this volume — an *«Antonium filium Bartholomæi **Moretti** Forojuliensem ex Gradisca»* marries on **14 February 1753**, frame 204. The correction rests on the letterforms at native resolution and on the comparison with a securely-read *Monaldi*, **not** on the surname being impossible here. *Said plainly because a correction that leans on an absence which turns out not to exist is worse than the error it replaced.*

**And a caution on the circle.** *Defranceschi–Spingarolli–Monaldi* has been read here as a pattern around this family. On **2 February 1752** (frame 201) **Nob. D.no Petro Monaldi and Nob. D.no Antonio Spingarolli witness together** at the wedding of a daughter of **Nob. D.no Josephi de Franchi** — a different family. The same pair witnesses for **de Franchi** again on 9 July 1752. **Monaldi and Spingarolli are the port's standing noble witnesses**, not a tie peculiar to this name. *The 1737 Monaldi at Valentino's wedding is still worth having; it is evidence of standing, not of kinship.*

**What this item has left.** Fiume is exhausted for the marriage question: both the volume and the index have now been asked and answered. The item stands where it stood — **Magdalena's maiden name**, in the County of Pazin's own books at the **Državni arhiv u Pazinu**. *An errand, not a read.*
